speech_en: Tick check — all clear up here!
speech_de: Zeckencheck – hier oben ist alles sauber!
scenario: A cheerful round tick character perched on a big spotted toadstool mushroom in a woodland clearing (ferns and a clover leaf around it), with a big friendly personified magnifying glass leaning in for a closer look — the everyday 'tick check' habit, deliberately different from the Borrelia page's grass-blade + tweezers-removal scene in this atlas.
status: RENDERED — accepted on attempt 3 with gemini-2.5-flash-image. Attempt 1 drew the tick with only 6 legs bunched in two small clusters. Attempt 2 (stronger 'exactly eight, evenly spaced' instruction) fixed the count but the legs rendered as an overlapping wavy fringe rather than eight separated legs, and the segmented rear body was lost. Attempt 3 (top-down 'simple cartoon spider' framing, four legs fanned left / four fanned right, explicit no-overlap instruction) produced a clean tick with exactly eight clearly separated legs and no border/starburst; accepted. Known compromise: the requested second character (a friendly pair of tweezers) did not render as tweezers in attempt 3 — it came out as a second grass/frond shape with a small face instead. Not re-rolled a 4th time because doing so risked losing the now-correct eight-leg count (per the sibling Borrelia lesson: don't re-roll a working anatomy fix to chase a secondary prop). The magnifying glass character rendered correctly in all three attempts.

prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) this is a ZOOMED-IN close-up composition — the mushroom, ferns and background elements must run past every edge of the square, filling the whole frame; (c) NO decorative starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays or sunbeam rays anywhere.

SCENE: A round, good-natured cartoon TICK is perched on top of a big spotted toadstool mushroom cap in a woodland clearing, surrounded by curling fern fronds and a chunky clover leaf. A big cheerful MAGNIFYING GLASS with a friendly face floats in from one side for a closer look — a "tick check" — while a large friendly pair of TWEEZERS peeks in from the opposite corner, ready to help. Playful and reassuring, never scary, no removal action happening yet — just a cheerful woodland moment.
- The TICK is drawn from directly ABOVE (top-down view, like a simple cartoon spider), seen sitting on the mushroom cap. It has one big smooth rounded oval body (no separate insect head — just a tiny fold near the front where the mouth is) with a simple friendly face (two round dot eyes and a small contented smile) near the front edge. Its EIGHT LEGS are drawn exactly like a simple children's-book spider's legs: four straight-ish legs splay out to the LEFT of the body and four straight-ish legs splay out to the RIGHT of the body, like the ribs of a fan, each leg a single simple bent line (thigh then foot) with clear white space between it and its neighbor — NO two legs touching or overlapping, NO wavy zigzag cluster, NO tight bunch. Count them as you draw: left side 1, 2, 3, 4 — right side 1, 2, 3, 4 — eight total, evenly fanned out from the sides of the body, not all crowded at one end.
- The MUSHROOM is a big, rounded toadstool with a domed, spotted cap (large simple circles for spots) and a thick stubby stem, taking up the lower-middle of the picture and running off the bottom edge.
- FERNS AND CLOVER: two or three large curling fern fronds with simple leaflets, and one chunky three-lobed clover leaf, fill the corners and edges of the picture, some cut off by the frame edges.
- The MAGNIFYING GLASS is huge and friendly: a round lens with a thick chunky handle, coming in from the upper corner, with a cheerful little face (two round eyes, a small smile) on its rim, as if leaning in for a closer look at the tick.
- The TWEEZERS are huge and friendly: two long tapering arms joined at a rounded hinge, coming in from another corner, blunt rounded tips slightly open, with a cheerful little face near the hinge — two round eyes and a small smile — so they read as a helpful friend on standby, not a threat.
- Everything is drawn LARGE, SIMPLE and CHUNKY, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — mushroom, ferns and clover are CUT OFF by the image edge itself.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — the mushroom stem, fern fronds and clover run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO blood, no bite wound, no red marks, no frightened or angry faces, nothing gruesome.
- NO human figure, no hand holding the magnifying glass or tweezers — they float in on their own as friendly characters.
- Do NOT draw only six legs on the tick — it must have eight short legs, all near the front of its body.
